title: Recursion & Backtracking Journey
description: Recursive contracts, subsets, permutations, duplicate handling, constraints, and search pruning.

journey.outcome: Define a recursive choice tree, restore shared state after each branch, and prune only when no valid completion remains.

connections.powx-n: Start with a recursive contract that reduces the problem rapidly. Compute one half-power and reuse it instead of evaluating the same recursive subproblem twice.
connections.subsets: Move from one recursive result to enumerating choices. Every item can be included or excluded, and an output snapshot must not alias the mutable path used by later branches.
connections.combinations: Restrict subset enumeration to a fixed number of choices. Increasing indices prevent reordered copies of the same combination, and remaining capacity can prune impossible branches.
connections.permutations: Now order matters, so a start index is insufficient. Track which positions are already used or swap choices into a fixed prefix, restoring changes after recursion.
connections.subsets-ii: Allow repeated input values without duplicating output subsets. Sorting lets you skip equal choices at the same recursion depth while still permitting repeated values along one path.
connections.combination-sum: Add a target total and allow a chosen candidate to be reused. Keeping the current choice index after selection distinguishes reusable choices from ordinary subsets.
connections.combination-sum-ii: Remove reuse while keeping duplicate input values. Advance the index after choosing an occurrence and skip equal siblings, not all later occurrences globally.
connections.generate-parentheses: Generate only prefixes that can still become balanced. Count opened and closed brackets; rejecting invalid prefixes early is stronger than generating every string and filtering afterward.
connections.letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number: Use one independent option set per position. A complete path chooses exactly one letter for each digit, and empty input needs the judge's empty-result behavior.
connections.word-search: Move the choice tree onto a board with adjacency constraints. Mark a cell only for the current path and restore it when leaving that branch.
connections.palindrome-partitioning: Choose whole substrings as edges of the search tree. Only palindromic pieces are legal, and precomputed palindrome tests can remove repeated validation work.
connections.n-queens: Track constraints that summarize all previous choices: occupied columns and diagonals. One queen per row fixes a dimension and prevents unnecessary permutations of identical placements.
connections.sudoku-solver: Interview stretch: combine reversible assignments with several simultaneous constraint sets. Choosing the empty cell with the fewest candidates can shrink the search dramatically without changing correctness.
